feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: Remembering Juan Atkins, known as the originator of techno
entry.summary: Detroit native Juan Atkins has died. He's known as the "godfather" or "originator" of techno music.

entry.title: Coal no longer king in Navajo Nation presidential election
entry.summary: For the first time in decades, there's no pro-coal candidate for Navajo Nation president. Coal has been an important part of the economy, but voter sentiment is changing.

entry.title: Archaeologists are using chemistry to learn more about mummies
entry.summary: Ancient Egyptian mummy remains were once marketed as medicine. Research finds at least some of these products came from real human remains and that mummy materials keep bodies preserved for millennia.

entry.title: Wars in Iran and Yemen dent Saudi modernization mega-projects
entry.summary: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's vision to transform the economy and draw tourists collides with his long-running war against Yemen's Houthis

entry.title: We all need sleep. Even spiders
entry.summary: New research suggests that spiders reach an active REM-like sleep state, similar to humans.

entry.title: With ACA open enrollment starting, healthcare is top of mind for many voters
entry.summary: Open enrollment for the Affordable Card Act marketplace opens Nov. 1, just two days before Election Day, putting healthcare in sharp focus the same year millions have lost coverage.

entry.title: Like it or not, the White House needs NATO to keep fighting in Iran
entry.summary: President Trump has had harsh words for NATO since the beginning of the war with Iran. Eight months later, the situation may be settling down, as NATO allies look for ways to take on a greater role.

entry.title: Why the freezer section is the new battleground in cyber security
entry.summary: Another wave of suspected cyberattacks targeted European supermarkets and fridges. NPR has been investigating what appears to be a pattern of similar attacks going back as far as the spring.

entry.title: Trump offered a closing message to voters by touting his D.C. renovations
entry.summary: In Washington, President Trump delivered his last expected public address, pushing a weaving message to the public about why they should support Republicans.

entry.title: A judge hears arguments about whether to dismiss Lindsay Clancy case
entry.summary: Prosecutors still have not said if they will seek to re-try Clancy after a mistrial was declared two months ago. The judge heard arguments on Monday that could decide Clancy's fate.
